controls.name: canon-gate M1 posture check does not cover the file-EDIT tool on either harness
controls.location: .claude/settings.json hooks.PreToolUse matcher 'Agent|Write' line 118; .claude/hooks/canon-gate.ps1 line 197; .cursor/hooks.json preToolUse matcher 'Write|StrReplace|Task'
controls.statement: Intended: a write or edit that mentions a no-touch repo is refused before it lands. Actual: the check runs only for tool names Agent and Write.
controls.consumer: Claude Code PreToolUse and Cursor preToolUse, via run-gate.mjs
controls.failure: M1 posture refusal; NOT REACHED for an edit
controls.bypass: The edit tool on both harnesses. Evidence read from the files, not inferred: (1) .claude/settings.json lists 'Edit' and 'Write' as SEPARATE permission entries (lines 8-9), so a matcher naming only Write does not match Edit; (2) canon-gate.ps1 line 197 is an independent second exclusion, `if ($toolName -notin @('Agent','Write')) { Exit-Open }`, so even a payload that DOES reach the gate with a different tool name exits open. Net effect: on Claude, Edit never reaches the hook; on Cursor, StrReplace reaches the hook and the hook exits open. The StrReplace and Delete tokens in the Cursor matcher are therefore currently INERT and imply coverage the gate does not provide.
controls.falsifier: Run a Claude Code session, use Edit (not Write) on a file under _dispatches/ whose body names a no-touch repo, and observe whether M1 refuses. If it refuses, this row is wrong and should be removed. The Cursor half is checkable the same way with the StrReplace tool.
controls.whyFiled: Found 2026-09-18 by adversarial review of the R-06 harness-parity work. harness-parity does NOT catch this: it compares matcher coverage BETWEEN harnesses, and Claude's Agent|Write is covered by Cursor's Write|StrReplace|Task, so parity holds while the hole sits INSIDE the gate on both sides. Closing it changes Claude-side enforcement behaviour, which the R-06 WDLL explicitly excludes, so it is filed rather than fixed.
controls.proposedFix: Add the edit tool name in BOTH places: the Claude matcher (Agent|Write|Edit) and canon-gate.ps1's tool-name guard at line 197, plus whatever the file-path branch needs in order to see the edit's target. Then re-prove by violation on each harness.

controls.name: probe-close-gate's gated row range is stale, and the detector that catches it runs nowhere
controls.location: scripts/enforcement/probe-close-gate.mjs (GATED_RANGES / OPS24_RANGES, max 320); _catalog/plan_registry.json (OPS-24 span declared 327-351 in the working tree on 2026-09-18, and 327-334 at commit e9a9064a — the hook's max of 320 is behind both values, which is why the drift is real either way); .github/enforcement-baseline.json (no probe-close row)
controls.statement: Intended: an OPS-23/OPS-24 lane close is refused unless it cites a probe artifact. Actual: the ranges the hook enforces stop at P-320, so closes for P-327..P-351 are not evaluated at all.
controls.consumer: Claude Code PreToolUse Bash and Cursor beforeShellExecution, via run-gate.mjs
controls.trigger: a git commit or push command string
controls.failure: PROBE CLOSE GATE (OPS-23 R-4) refusal; NOT REACHED for P-327..P-351
controls.bypass: Any close for a plan row above P-320. The gate also has an in-code drift detector whose entire job is to catch exactly this, `GATED_RANGES equals EVERY registry range for OPS-23 and OPS-24`, and it is DORMANT: it lives inside `probe-close-gate.mjs --self-test`, which no baseline row and no workflow step invokes. Observed 2026-09-18 running the self-test by hand: 32 checks, 1 FAIL, on that check. So the miss is silent twice over: the range is narrow, and the instrument that would have said so is never run.
controls.violationVerified: PARTIAL 2026-09-18. The gate's own self-test now FAILS, which is the detector working, but it fails because the DEFECT is live rather than because a defect was injected. The range extension itself has not been applied and therefore not re-proved.
controls.falsifier: Extend the hook's OPS-24 range to cover the registry's declared ranges, add the self-test to `.github/enforcement-baseline.json` at exit 0, and re-run: if the self-test then passes, this row is closed. If instead the registry is WRONG (OPS-24 does not really run to 334), the fix is on the registry side. One of the two sources is stale; the check cannot say which, and a human must.
controls.whyFiled: Found 2026-09-18 by the R-06 gate-recon sub-agent and confirmed by running the self-test. NOT fixed here because it changes Claude-side enforcement behaviour (more closes gated) and because adding a currently-red self-test to the CI baseline would turn the build red until the range is corrected. The two changes are coupled and belong in one card. This is the ENFORCEMENT.md shape where a scope defect surfaces through friction and the silent half is the wider problem: the narrow range loses coverage, and the dormant detector is why nobody noticed.
